full_judgment:
2. The petitioner as first party filed petition before the Upazila Magistrate against the accused party opposite party Nos. 1-5 claiming that he is in possession and enjoying the case plot No. 281 of Khatian No. 104 and area of 3.42 acres of land half of the said case land was purchased by him and her brothers through registered kabala deeds and the remaining half was exchanged from the owners. He took possession of the case land along with his brothers and enjoying and possessing the same by growing paddy regularly. In the last year they grew boro paddy which was ripe for harvesting but the opposite parties who failed to purchase the land became hostile to the petitioner and on the 15th April. 1985 at about 09:00/10:00 AM came to the land armed with lathi, sulfi and formed an unlawful assembly and attacked the petitioner in the case land. But due to the intervention of the neighboring people they left the place. The opposite parties constantly threatening the petitioner to dispossess and cut the paddy grown by him and there arose apprehension of serious breach of peace over the case land and due to this constant threat of the opposite parties he could not peacefully harvest the paddy and as such appropriate steps should be taken against the opposite parties restraining them not to interfere with the possession of the petitioner in the case land. 

 7. He also discussed the evidence of the second party opposite parties and he found out their case on the basis of their evidence and the documents they filed before the court. Their case is that they purchased land from Sonai, Bairagi and Umesh Bairagi the plots of land being plot No. 317 and 318 comprising an area of 3.36 acres under khatian No. 104, the record was subsequently corrected by filing the Misc. Case before the ADC (Rev) Sylhet and accordingly, they also claimed the case plot No. 281 comprising an area of 3.42 acres. The first party purchased this half of the case land from the original owners and the rest half by exchange of the property from Sontosh Sarker and Sunil Sarker and since then they are in possession of the property. From the evidence on record it was found that there is a transfer of the land with the first party who is in possession of the case land and there is dispute with the second party in respect of the possession of the same land. He came to finding that the first party is in possession of the property and there is an apprehension of the breach of peace in respect of the possession of the land and so he ordered not to disturb the possession of the first party by the second party.
